description: Interactive tool for teaching the Simultaneous Division Method to find HCF (Highest Common Factor) and LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) of two numbers. Aligned with Ganita Prakash Grade 7 Chapter 3.

showNavigation.description: Show/hide prev/next buttons and step indicator

filterSteps.description: Array of step IDs to show (null = show all)

additionalProps.description: Tool-specific dynamic content passed by the agent to customize the numbers used in the simultaneous division method

numberA.description: First number for learn mode HCF/LCM calculation

numberB.description: Second number for learn mode HCF/LCM calculation

practiceNumberA.description: First number for practice mode (student fills in divisors)

practiceNumberB.description: Second number for practice mode (student fills in divisors)

learn.description: Step-by-step walkthrough of simultaneous division method showing how to find HCF and LCM. Includes Guna's shortcut (dividing by HCF directly).

practice.description: Student fills in the common prime divisors for practiceNumberA and practiceNumberB. Answers are validated with feedback.

1.title: The Division Table
1.description: Introduction with real-world context (vegetable market packing problem). Shows the two numbers.

2.title: Divide by 2
2.description: First division step — divides both numbers by 2.

3.title: Divide by 2 Again
3.description: Second division step — divides quotients by 2 again.

4.title: Divide by 3
4.description: Third division step — divides quotients by 3.

5.title: Stop! No More Common Primes
5.description: Identifies when to stop (no more shared prime factors).

6.title: Read Off the HCF
6.description: Shows HCF = product of left column divisors.

7.title: Read Off the LCM
7.description: Shows LCM = product of all divisors × bottom row remainders.

8.title: Guna's Shortcut!
8.description: Alternative: divide by HCF directly in one step instead of prime-by-prime.

10.title: Your Turn
10.description: Student inputs divisors for practiceNumberA and practiceNumberB. Validated on submit.

decisionTree.description: Decision tree for agents to determine which parameters to use

rules.trigger: Student asks 'What is simultaneous division?' or 'How to find HCF and LCM?'
Student asks 'Find HCF and LCM of [A] and [B]'
rules.action: Use: initialMode: 'learn', additionalProps: { numberA: A, numberB: B }

rules.trigger: Student asks to practice or 'Let me try'
rules.action: Use: initialMode: 'practice', additionalProps: { practiceNumberA: A, practiceNumberB: B }

rules.trigger: Student asks about Guna's shortcut or 'Is there a faster way?'
Teacher wants minimal distractions for assessment
rules.action: Use: initialMode: 'practice', showModeSelector: false, showNavigation: false

rules.trigger: Student needs a specific step explained again
rules.action: Use: filterSteps: [stepId], showNavigation: false, showModeSelector: false

errorHandling.invalidNumbers: If numberA or numberB are less than 2, or not integers, the division table will be empty. Always use integers >= 2.
errorHandling.coprimeNumbers: If the two numbers share no common factor (e.g., 7 and 15), the division table will be empty and HCF = 1. This is valid behavior.
errorHandling.invalidMode: If initialMode is not 'learn' or 'practice', defaults to 'learn'.
errorHandling.emptyAdditionalProps: If no additionalProps are provided, defaults to numberA=84, numberB=180, practiceNumberA=300, practiceNumberB=150.
errorHandling.filterStepsEmpty: If filterSteps is an empty array or contains no matching IDs, no content will be shown. Always include valid step IDs.

tipsForAgents: For learn mode, the steps are tied to the default numbers (84 and 180). Step descriptions reference specific divisions (÷2, ÷2, ÷3). If you change numberA/numberB, the table content adapts but the step descriptions still reference the default example text.
For practice mode, always choose numbers that share at least one common prime factor, otherwise the table will be empty.
Use filterSteps to show only relevant steps when answering a specific question (e.g., 'What is HCF?' → filterSteps: [6]).
Set showModeSelector: false when you want the student to focus on one mode only.
Set showNavigation: false for single-step views (combined with filterSteps).
The practice mode validates divisors exactly — the student must enter primes in the correct order (smallest first, repeated as needed).
Guna's Shortcut (step 8) teaches that dividing by any common factor (not just primes) works. It's a great follow-up after the main method.
For a complete lesson flow: start with learn mode (all steps), then switch to practice mode.
Both numbers must be positive integers >= 2 for meaningful results.
